title: Product Color Variations in a Coordinated Set | AIVideosUGC
description: Create one coordinated photo for every product color from your own shade photos, so shoppers can compare options in the same scene. Square AI images.
h1: Product Color Variations for a Coordinated Photo Set
lead: Swatch names hide how a finish looks in context. Show every product color in one coordinated square set so shoppers can compare options.

steps.d: Attach one clear photo of the actual shade, with the whole item and texture in frame. Real sources keep finishes honest.
Describe the setting and camera once and apply it to every source. Each square image keeps its true shade.
Download each image, compare the hue with the real item, then link it to its option. Shoppers get a clean comparison.

faq.q: How do I keep color options consistent?
faq.a: The set uses a shared view, light and background so shoppers compare the finish instead of a changing setup.

faq.q: Can the tool create a different product color?
faq.a: It can render a described color change, but a generated shade is not a substitute for a photo of the real option.

faq.q: Where should each variation image go?
faq.a: Attach each downloaded image to its matching product option in a listing gallery, feed post or carousel.

faq.q: Do I need a photo for each color?
faq.a: For reliable shade matching, use a clear source photo of each actual color, especially when dye, glaze, fabric or finish changes.

faq.q: Will the generated colors match my real products?
faq.a: Review every result against the physical item or swatch. Use the real product photo when exact shade matters.
Each variation photo costs 24 credits, and the total appears before you create the set.

faq.q: Can the tool invent a new color from one photo?
faq.a: It can show a color concept, but selling an option calls for a photo of that actual shade and a review against the sample.

faq.q: Do I need a reshoot for every color variation?
faq.a: No. Once the real shades are photographed, the same coordinated scene can be applied without repeat styled shoots.

steps.prompt: Place the uploaded dispenser on a clean white surface with its shade unchanged.

steps_h2: How to make color variation photos in 3 simple steps
steps_lead: Three steps turn your shade photos into a coordinated option set - no repeat shoots, no mismatched supplier shots.
